judges.17.p1.b1.text: Now a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim

judges.17.p1.b2.text: The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you … I have the silver here with me; I took it.

judges.17.p1.b3.text: Blessed be my son by the LORD!

judges.17.p1.b4.text: I wholly dedicate the silver to the LORD for my son’s benefit, to make a graven image and a molten idol.

judges.17.p2.b1.text: she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a graven image and a molten idol.

judges.17.p2.b2.text: Now this man Micah had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols, and ordained one of his sons as his priest.

judges.17.p2.b3.text: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

judges.17.p3.b1.text: And there was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who had been residing within the clan of Judah. … to settle where he could find a place.

judges.17.p3.b3.text: I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, … and I am on my way to settle wherever I can find a place.

judges.17.p3.b4.text: Stay with me, … and be my father and priest, and I will give you ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of clothes, and your provisions.

judges.17.p4.b1.text: and agreed to stay with him, and the young man became like a son to Micah.

judges.17.p4.b2.text: Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.

judges.17.p4.b3.text: Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because a Levite has become my priest.
